root_cause.text: In ntfs3's ntfs_get_frame_pages(), newly allocated frame folios could be returned uninitialized because they were created without zeroing and, when ni_read_frame() was skipped under the assumption of full overwrite, partially written folios left unread portions containing uninitialized memory later consumed by compression code.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that “new folios are allocated without being marked uptodate and ni_read_frame() is skipped” so “some reserved folios may remain only partially filled, leaving the rest memory uninitialized,” and the fix adds `__GFP_ZERO` to `__filemap_get_folio(...)` in `ntfs_get_frame_pages()` to initialize those folios before use.

intent_record.how: This causes newly created folios obtained through __filemap_get_folio() to be zero-initialized on allocation, preventing uninitialized memory from being present in newly allocated page cache folios used by this NTFS path.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the full body of the relevant function `ntfs_get_frame_pages()` and its call sites in `ntfs_compress_write()`, so it is sufficient to judge the vulnerable logic. In `ntfs_get_frame_pages()`, pages are obtained only via `find_or_create_page(mapping, index, gfp_mask);` and then the code merely checks `if (!PageUptodate(page)) *frame_uptodate = false;` before returning them in `pages[npages] = page;`. There is no zeroing or initialization of newly created pages in this function. The root cause describes newly allocated frame folios/pages being returned uninitialized, and that later `ni_read_frame()` may be skipped under a full-overwrite assumption. That exact pattern is present in `ntfs_compress_write()`: after `ntfs_get_frame_pages(...)`, if `!frame_uptodate`, the code reads existing data only conditionally: `if (off || (to < i_size && (to & (frame_size - 1)))) { err = ni_read_frame(...); }`. Therefore when a frame is not uptodate but the write is assumed to fully overwrite the needed region, `ni_read_frame()` is skipped. The subsequent copy loop writes only the user-supplied bytes into the pages (`copy_page_from_iter_atomic(...)`), after which the whole frame is passed to `ni_write_frame(ni, pages, pages_per_frame);`. Because `ntfs_get_frame_pages()` did not zero newly created pages, any portions of those pages/frame not covered by the user copy can remain uninitialized and then be consumed by compression/writeback logic.
